item.title: Re: Aboriginal Australian Culture and Dreamtime
item.content:encoded:
Disclaimer: I am not an aboriginal Australian. I do not claim to be an expert on their culture/practices

After reading a bit into the cultural impact of Koalas I found a connection to dreamtime on the Wikipedia page for Koalas, quote:

The Tharawal people believed that the animal helped row the boat that brought them to the continent.[140] Another myth tells of how a tribe killed a koala and used its long intestines to create a bridge for people from other parts of the world. This narrative highlights the koala's status as a game animal and the length of its intestines.

So at least two koala myths connect to travel between continents, which is an interesting connection. In terms of ceremonies that occur, I would recommend reading this article, as it lists a lot of ceremonies. Hope this helps!

In mathematics, a complement is the set of elements that complete a universal set that are not part of the set in question, eg, an oblate spheroid.

I know this is a mistake, but this line implies that the shape of 5127 is all R3 embedded shapes that are not an oblate spheroid, which I think is a weirdly fascinating idea.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: “Patient Zero”
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Fiction

Elevator Pitch: SCP-5968 is an anomalous humanoid who has a strange immunity to the effects of some of the foundation’s most dangerous SCP’s and has shown the ability of nullifying the anomalous properties of said SCP’s. They are not anomalous in any ways other than immunity and nullification. No super strength; no super intelligence; no super powers.

Central Narrative: Numerous addendums describing studies and tests involving SCP-5968’s interactions with and reactions to other SCP’s. Some data is still in progress, and the storyline for INCIDENT-5968/H is TBD.

Hook/Attention Grabber: SCP-5968 is both one of the most helpful, and most dangerous, anomalies at the foundation. We know how he is helpful, but what makes him so dangerous?

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) The Uncontainable Man
item.content:encoded:
I'll be honest, I've seen lots of attempts at the same sort of premise. Most of the time the audience isn't much of a fan, especially if you're pairing the already arrogant overpowered main character with the Foundation being extremely incompetent (the situation you're describing in the narrative seems to necessitate an extreme waste of resources and personnel. It would make much more sense for the Foundation to either convince the guy that he wants to remain in whatever low-cost containment is reasonable for him, or just keep him rendered comatose 24/7).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Explores what would actually happen if the Foundation encountered an anomaly whose property is that he cannot be contained

We already have a lot of anomalies with similar properties. You can use the Tag Search tool to search up the pages tagged with "uncontained".

If you intend to focus on the comedic aspects of the Foundation being incompetent, I could potentially see this working as a tale, but the premise of curbstomping Mary Sues has already been addressed many times on the site, like in the Resurrection series where an agent shoots a reality bender, the joke article where Foundation personnel review and downvote a powerful anomalous being, tales like Eldritch Application, and so on. You would need to have something significantly different and unique to make this stand out amongst the existing material.

item.title: Seeking greenlights (Ghost Rider)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Horror
Elevator Pitch: My idea of the SCP is a possessed vehicle that starts driving around from midnight till sunrise. The vehicle drives in unpopulated areas with a very loud sound that reaches houses miles away. If an unlucky individual happens to see the car it will try to run over that individual, however, if that individual survives until sunrise then the car would shutdown forgetting about him, going out looking for new individuals on the next day on midnight.
Central Narrative: The story starts when Andy, a young10 year old boy was living his life around abusive people, but always loved the car his father has down in his garage. Every time Andy wanted to sleep, the distant sound of a car driving always helps him get sleepy enough to fall asleep. Once after a fight with his father at midnight, Andy got the car and drove of into a far unpopulated area where he met the unfortunate death crashing to a tree. Andy ended up possessing the car and it is said he drives off from midnight till sunrise looking for individuals to run over, therefore if you hear a car from your home after midnight do not go outside whatsoever.
Hook/Attention Grabber: Many times when sleeping you can hear a car driving with a loud sound in the middle of the night, that might make you confused or scared. This vehicle is the car that produces that sound, try to stay away from the sound and do not look outside the window if you hear it.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea - Security Blanket
item.content:encoded:
Hello Blackvvwater! lets take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A young orphan boy is found in possession of a quilt with anomalous properties. He is also being stalked by anomalous entities who wish to take the blanket from him.

My main issue, is there doesn't seem to be much of a connection between the quilt and the entities attached to it. Which as a result, makes the concept feel disjointed and hard to get invested in. Along with this, there isn't much context to why or how this is happening, which makes the skip feel close to a "thing that does a thing".- why should I as the reader care about the concept? what makes this idea stand out for similar premises? what give this an edge?

Another major issue I have is the blankets anomaly; there doesn't seem to be any limit to what it can do, it can literally get whoever posses it out of any danger whatsoever. As result there's no real conflict or attention grabbing elements, as any possible threats are immediately stopped with no time to really develop.- I would highly recommend you either have the blanket with one or two anomalies or put some sort of limit/restriction on how it operates.

The narrative:

Central Narrative: An MTF team is sent to a small farmhouse where anomalous events have been reported. During their sweep the team a young boy appears out of nowhere, clutching a quilt with strange designs. The MTF team convince the boy to accompany them back to a site, where the boy is interviewed by SCP personnel.

The boy reveals that his grandmother, who recently died, gave him the quilt, explaining that it would protect him. Study of the quilt reveals that the designs on it are thaumaturgical symbols of protection, and while in the boy's possession, it displays a number of functions. When he hides under it, the boy cannot be perceived. When wrapped around him, the quilt protects him from physical harm. It can also slowly heal wounds. When he ties it around his neck like a cape, it allows the boy to fly. What's more, while the boy can willingly surrender the quilt, if it's forcibly taken, it returns to him in a matter of moments.

During his detainment, the boy also explains that the quilt protects him from "the bad things." These "bad things" are anomalous entities that manage to penetrate the site and seem to exhibit ghost-like abilities. SCP personnel discover that they're drawn to the blanket rather than the boy, as the child exhibits no anomalous qualities. The "bad things" also appear blind to the quilt when it's inert, so it's simply a matter of encouraging the child to surrender the quilt. However, SCP personnel find it difficult to convince him to give up the last thing connecting him to his family.

Currently it doesn't feel like there's any building tension, nothing is really leading to a payoff or big reveal, which makes the story feel rather anticlimactic. None of the questions that the concept raised are answered here either, as I'm still unsure on what these entities are, why the skip has the blanket to begin with, what the entities motives are and what the the Foundations motives are.

Overall, the base ideas shown in the concept aren't expanded upon much, which makes the story feel anticlimactic. The storyline also feels a bit cliched and flat as it doesn't give much other than "Foundation finds something, then tests it".- what will make this narrative interesting? what about it will make the audience invested? who are the characters (this can include the skip itself)? how will they make me as the reader feel?

This is what I'd recommend;

-'Security blankets' are not a new concept, they have likely been done here before, and if they aren't given enough care, they could end up falling into a cliche; you will need to make sure that this puts a unique spin on the premise, try looking through similar concepts in other articles (or even offsite), as they can help with inspiration and comparison, and they allow for you to study how others may have pulled off a similar idea.

- Cut out the entities or give them a strong motive to be after the blanket; currently they feel like a device to create tension as they don't seem connected to the concept, and thy don't play much of a part in the narrative, they are one of the only threats to the blanket. From what I can see, not much (if anything) would need to change if they were removed.

- Nerf the blankets anomalies, and give it more context; this thing is far too powerful, and as a result any possible conflicts are quelled before they can really start. Along with this the blankets origins aren't really given much of an explanation, it doesn't seem to have any real reason to exist, other than to protect the boy (which on its own won't really stand), there needs to be a reason to protect to boy.

That said, if you want any additional feedback (for this or any concept), feel welcome to send a PM. (response times generally range from 2-12 hrs). If your looking for additional feedback, then I would highly recommend the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

RED

item.title: THE GREAT REVIEW: ELECTRIC BOOGALOO
item.content:encoded:
Greetings! If you don't know who I am, I'm Jak. As DarkStuff alluded to in their post, they may be a bit busy with other things. So, in order to help them and to also make sure that everyone has their gifts reviewed before the 29th, I have offered to step in and help with the remaining articles. But hey, if you were looking forward to DarkStuff's review then no worries! They have said that they will get to everyones eventually. Even if it meant going beyond the 29th to read/review them all. So, with that being said: let the reviews continue! (Please note that I also will more-than-likely lack the proper context for most of these articles. So, consider this a fresh pair of eyes!)

Connor MacWarren's Gift
A Working Theory

This is a tale relating to MacWarren's author avatar, Dr. Connor MacWarren. The tale itself was somewhat difficult for me to follow through parts but definitely a worthwhile read. I really enjoyed the characterization of Dr. MacWarren and his interactions with the other personnel, and the climax with the tunnel generator failing was really fun. I also liked Dr. Pheonix's interjections throughout, even if they did feel somewhat confusing and misplaced at first. The ending concluded at a rather decent hook, leaving me wondering exactly what the file that the Memetics Department was keeping away from Dr. Henshaw was really all about. I'd argue that this was missing some further fleshing out, but that shouldn't detract from what's there now (and it's definitely interesting). Despite that, and some minor tone/SPaG errors, I had a lot of fun with this!

Deadly Bread's Gift
Where the Smoke Trail Ends

This is an SCP document relating to Fifthism, memes, cross-anomalous contamination, and SCP-5993. Although I hate to admit it, I am definitely missing some context with this article. Being still new to the concept of Fifthism, and not having read SCP-5993, it was hard for me to really follow at points. That being said, this is some high quality work. The clinical tone is really nice, and the incorporation of the multiple Departments and crosslinks related to Fifthism was fun. I really enjoyed the ending, after finally figuring out what had happened to allow an anomaly like this to occur. The addenda really stack onto another nicely and coherently. I loved the Experiment/Unusual incidents as well since they really brought out this concept well. And that picture. Great usage of media to help really tie together the ending. Bravo!

Ethagon's Gift
Explanation and Research Department

This is a very creative gift: A Site-Dossier for a "Explanation and Research Department" (EXaRD). Frankly, the only upsetting part of this article is the amount of information that simply couldn't be shared—whether that be from things still not being determined yet, or simply having no extra content that helps tie it together. HOWEVER. What is there is nothing short of impressing. I am incredibly excited to see this get updated and posted. I love the in-depth Site Overview with the separate Research, Reclassification, and Release initiatives being amazingly intriguing. Honestly the entire prospect of this Department and its interactions with -EX anomalys is super sweet, and this Dossier compliments that by a large, large margin. It's clear, concise, and I can tell that a lot of detail definitely went into it in order to make it seem real. Can't wait to see this fleshed out and expanded upon by each of you!

LordStonefish's Gift
Here be Gifts!

This is a very interesting tale surrounding the Glittering Horizons Series. Admittedly, I really lack the context surrounding the series of events with Van Turner, the Department of Photography, and everything else. Regardless, this was an extremely fun little piece. I personally enjoyed the duality between Van Turner's proposal towards the Council and Joseph being chased down by his mysterious gunman. The action between the two was definitely there and really kept me engaged throughout. The progression between the two also really flowed well for me, and the ending definitely left me wondering. Why did they do this? What's the bigger play at hand here? What's the real reason behind this all? A wonderful piece narratively, with smooth prose and detailed imagery to really nail things together. Great job author!

Lt Flop's Gift
Team Bird!!!

This Is lovely art for the Team Bird Series! I must say: this art is super beautiful. From the linework to the little details of the background, it all works together really well. The colors are really nice, with the added texture really tying it all together. I am very interested to see what the hieroglyphics mean behind the pigeons and on the side of the piece itself. Thoth himself looks super nice, with the pose really matching that of other ancient Egyptian pieces (or so I've seen). All-in-all, this is a very cute piece of art. Like I said, I adore the detail and the overall style and feel of it as a whole. Fantastic work!

Raptie's Gift
KTO-0001-Bellfather

This is an astonishing GOC article that flips the Foundation on-top of its head. First, the content warning: please heed it. Okay, going into the article itself: I'm blown away. This concept, just on its face, has so much potential. I love the idea behind the Foundation just being a rag-tag conglomeration of all the GoI's unilaterally hating the Coalition. "Keep your enemies closer," and all of that. I love the detail and synopsis of each of the Bellfather members. You can tell that a ton of time has been reserved for figuring out how to implement the differing characters and their involvement with the Foundation's directive. The format that it follows with the messages really helps the reader follow along with the article, with the ending being just so captivating. Seriously people, expand upon this. Characterizing the Overwatch Command like this could really lead to so much more good content. It also kinda revitalizes the "Foundation is evil" vibe that I've always digged. Good, good job author!

ROUNDERHOUSE's Gift
Wonder

This is a beautiful article concerning the insight of the narrator's "wonder" with man—taking place within the universe of the Wanderer's Library. Firstly, I am thoroughly blown away by the prose. All of the sentences flow really well together, each having a powerful impact onto another as the story progresses. The structure, tone, and diction of the paragraphs really amplifies the narrator, all while providing a vivid depiction of how this entity perceives man. It dives into our goods and bads, our highs and lows, and our grandest achievements over the minor successes. This piece definitely inspires awe and wonder, giving the reader a chance to see ourselves through a different metaphorical lens. It's absolutely beautiful. I really hope this get's posted on the Wanderers Library because wow. An impressive piece!

item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
{manifests again in response to PM}

Okay, this is going to be a bit of a back-and forth dialogue if you really want to forge this idea into shape, but since you seem serious about it let's dig in:

+ sculpture is still under the rock
- more chiseling

one of the critiques that I get here is that the one ability I do mention (instantly knowing things about stuff he sees) is boring/uninteresting or broken.

To put it simply, they're right. That can be fixed, though.

Firstly, heed Quadraginta's critique in particular- the traits they're pointing to are part of that Edgelord Canyon I mentioned you're trying to tightrope across. You might never win them over, but they're pointing out a lot of the pitfalls you need to avoid. (De-emphasizing the middle name to an initial is a good first move, for instance- was going to mention that being a little on-the-nose in the previous critique myself and forgot.)

Two things in your reply above sort of… bracket both what I've actually been finding interesting about this guy and what you'll want to avoid. I think it might be backwards from what you're thinking, though:

It's not going to be a batman utility belt scenario.

This is actually the less important of the two things, but Batman and his utility belt are a really good example to follow for this guy's collection of anomalies.

We're never told explicitly what's in the utility belt, and with Batman's resources and skills the options are pretty much limited only by what can plausibly fit in the belt. What good Batman writers figure out, though, is that the utility belt is boring when Batman has a gadget that does anything he needs to do for him. Used at its best, the belt always has what Batman needs to do anything in the most interesting way possible.

Same thing here: even you as the writer don't need to know every item Twist has. He can have whatever you want him to have- so long as it's in the name of doing something in the most interesting way possible. That's why I suggested emphasizing that most of his collection are innocuous and/or useless seeming items- they're things that only he would see the potential in. It's boring if he has a gizmo that lets him fly. It's interesting if he combines three minor anomalies in an way that causes him to be hurled through the air havok-physics-glitch style.

I haven't mentioned them because they aren't crucial to the story or to what the story is supposed to be focusing on, which is supposed to be about the SCP foundation trying to get information out of Twist and figuring out the rules to obtaining this information.

Again, the power isn't the interesting part, and the whole "the Foundation NEEDS the information" thing is a bit of a site cliche with oracles. (They might like to have said information, but there's loads of other POIs they'd love to put under a microscope, too.) I'd actually even suggest toning it down further, so that he doesn't have instant absolute insight into everything- if he just gets incomplete flashes and glimpses of insight its both a great narrative tool for foreshadowing and "how we got here" storytelling, and a much less "game-breaking" power.

Vincent Anderson of Anderson Robotics might be a good bit of site lore to look at regarding one way you could approach telling this guy's story. He's a literal cyborg sorcerer with all the makings of a stereotypical edgelord OC by the end of his arc- but his messy, complicated story about a man trying to find an offramp on that road paved with good intentions makes him one of the most interesting characters on the site. In Twist, you've got a similar chance to show us a really simple, fairly weak precognitive/clairvoyant type power leading a guy down the road to become one of the SCPverse's many boogymen.

item.title: First SCP: An Interdimensional Internet Router
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Technological, Interdimensional, Mystery

Page Layout (Optional): Article followed by session logs

Elevator Pitch: A normal looking internet router that when connected to will connect your devices to the internet of a similar dimension or timeline to our own.

Central Narrative: These will have varying differences in terms of technological advancement, society, politics, geography, evolutionary psychology, et cetera. The only definite similarity to our reality being that each would have technologically progressed to the point of inventing their version of the internet. Each instance of a dimension will change every time the router is rebooted or powered down.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There will be a log of sessions recorded by staff that have used this SCP to observe these realities and the differences in them. The reader can see instances of realities twith only minor differences (such as an instance where the US won the Vietnam War), to those that vary massively in a range of aspects (such as an instance where the continent Pangea never broke apart, and a species analogous to Humans evolved and formed societies and nations, with warfare being rarer due to differences in evolutionary psychology, and had progressed to a similar era with technology such as the internet).

Those examples were only quick ideas and aren't definite.

Additional Notes: I already began working on the draft as I had rushed into it, being unaware that I needed approval first. I hope that is fine, and you guys will find this to be an interesting (and original) idea for an SCP.

item.title: Re: Star Euthanizer
item.content:encoded:
Because Quad has already given you his once over, I will be going more in depth with the tone. I can already say I agree with what Quad has said, so I will be expanding on that. Without further ado!

It's time for some critique.
Hope it helps.

Page one

All telescopes capable of deep-space astrophotography are monitored by satellite following standard procedure.

This sentence reads a little weird to me. I would recommend changing it. Also keep in mind that you will need to change these on the other pages as well.

"All deep-space observatories are to be monitored by satellite following standard procedure."

The production and selling of new telescope parts such as refractors have been limited to companies where a sufficient number of undercover Foundation personnel is present.

Just a couple of word changes would hep this flow a bit better.

"The production and selling trade of new telescope parts such as refractors have been limited to companies where a sufficient number of undercover Foundation personnel is are present.

All images of SCP-XXXX are intercepted by the Foundation AI "Binary star", saved in the Foundation database, and subsequently deleted from public records. Witnesses must be administered Class B amnestics.

Same with this one.

"All images of SCP-XXXX are to be intercepted by the Foundation AI "Binary star", saved in the Foundation database, and subsequently deleted from public records. Witnesses must Those who witness the anomaly are to be administered Class B amnestics.

Page two

The exact composition cannot be confirmed due to the inability to take a sample.

I would change this slightly.

"The exact composition cannot be confirmed due to the inability to take difficulty in acquiring a sample.

SCP-XXXX is the object where the first zeppelin blueprints are based on.

Just one word.

"SCP-XXXX is the object where that the first zeppelin blueprints are based on.

On 4 December 1872, Ferdinand von Zeppelin claimed to have seen an oblate spheroid spaceship from a telescope.

I know you said that you would change this, but I think it should stay this way. Adds a bit of historical accuracy that gives this article a nice flavor. There is one change though.

"On 4 December 1872, Ferdinand von Zeppelin claimed to have seen an oblate spheroid spaceship from a with his telescope."

The Foundation administered him with amnestics. Due to the lesser quality of amnestics at the time, Ferdinand von Zeppelin did not suffer from complete memory-loss and had a few fragments left of SCP-XXXX in his subconsciousness.

This sentence can be structured in a better way.

"The Foundation He was administered him with amnestics. , however due to the lesser quality of amnestics at the time, Ferdinand von Zeppelin did not suffer from complete memory-loss and had a few fragments left of SCP-XXXX in his subconsciousness."

the Foundation decided to let von Zeppelin invent new aircraft with undercover personnel besides him as manual laborers.

Some more suggestions.

"the Foundation decided to let allow von Zeppelin to invent new aircraft with undercover personnel besides him planted as manual laborers."

It was anticipated that von Zeppelin eventually would develop a scaled-down version of SCP-XXXX.

I would switch the words ""eventually" and "would" in this sentence.

"It was anticipated that von Zeppelin would eventually develop a scaled-down version of SCP-XXXX."

On 28 August 1903, several researchers educated in astrology sighted SCP-XXXX

I feel like you could cut some of this sentence. Sense I would assume researchers searching for SCP-XXXX know a thing or two about astrology.

"On 28 August 1903, several researchers educated in astrology sighted SCP-XXXX-"

Page three

Personnel with Level 5 Clearance may use the Diplomat Terminal to view the communication logs with SCP-XXXX-1.

"may" doesn't sound very clinical. I would recommend changing this to "are allowed to".

"Personnel with Level 5 Clearance may are allowed to use the Diplomat Terminal to view the communication logs with SCP-XXXX-1."

SCP-XXXX is a dark metallic spacecraft roaming through space with one passenger on board, designated SCP-XXXX-1. SCP-XXXX serves as a transportation vessel and vault for SCP-XXXX-1.

This can be trimmed down some.

"SCP-XXXX is a dark metallic spacecraft roaming through space with one passenger on board, designated SCP-XXXX-1. SCP-XXXX that serves as a transportation vessel and vault for SCP-XXXX-1."

SCP-XXXX-1 "Glen" is an entity from which age nor origin have been successfully investigated.

One word change here.

"SCP-XXXX-1 "Glen" is an entity from which whose age nor origin have been successfully investigated."

-and store it inside of SCP-XXXX.

Don't think the "of" fits there.

"and store it inside of SCP-XXXX."

SCP-XXXX-1 is very knowledgeable about space and space-navigation in general to the extent that it can leap several lightyears worth of distance in mere minutes.

I think you can trim some fat here because you can already infer that SCP-XXXX-1 is knowledgeable about space.

"SCP-XXXX-1 is very knowledgeable about space and space-navigation in general to the extent that it can leap capable of leaping several lightyears worth of distance in mere minutes."

Due to the distance and interference, it took the message one week to reach Earth/SCP-XXXX-1. Below are the full communication logs with SCP-XXXX-1 from the terminal.

Some trimming.

"Due to the distance and interference, it took the message one week to reach Earth/SCP-XXXX-1. Below are the full communication logs with SCP-XXXX-1 from the terminal."

- GLEN, SCP-XXXX-1, THE RESETTER OF THE UNIVERSE

| CONNECTION BROKEN MANUALLY
| END HISTORY

I love this. That is why I recommend cutting everything after this. Like Quad said, I like the idea of a good god patrolling space protecting us, but I feel like this would be a far more impactful ending.

All in all I like this article a lot. To answer the questions you proposed on the forum I will say that the 2nd page is fine, your dialogue is great, and I love the twist. The one thing I would recommend thinking about is a way of making the text that has been added over the various iterations of the article pop out more. I have seen articles change the color of new text to blue or red, and I think it could work with this. I would also recommend getting some more critique. This is very close to something great, but there is probably things Quad and I have missed. I hope this was helpful and good luck.

item.title: Fireproof Rescue Dog
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Containment Procedures, Description, Recovered Incident Reports, Email Transcript

Genre: Dramatic, with some lighthearted moments between the dog and it’s handler

Elevator Pitch:

+ Show Elevator Pitch
- Hide Elevator Pitch

This SCP is a former SAR (Search and Rescue) dog that is completely unaffected by fire and smoke. When irritated, the dog is also able to raise its internal body temperature to an unnaturally high level, allowing it to essentially burn those who come into contact with it. Visually, the dog is a completely average looking dalmatian. Given that it was an SAR animal, the dog had a handler. However, the handler was entirely non-anomalous and the dog’s anomalous protection did not extend to them nor anything other than itself.

Central Narrative:

+ Show Central Narrative
- Hide Central Narrative

The central narrative of this SCP Article would be the history of the SCP’s life prior to containment. This would be told through SAR incident reports recovered by the Foundation, detailing calls the dog was used on and how the dog and it’s handler performed. The reports would be written by the dog’s handler and would detail their specific experiences working with the dog during the incident.

The dog is contained by the Foundation after it gives several children second and third degree burns. This result is from the dog spitting on and biting the children when they irritated it.

This incident is what alerts the Foundation to the dog’s existence. The dog is subsequently contained, with it’s handler and any witnesses to the incident anesthetized.

The article would end several years after the dog is contained, with a researcher in charge of the animal noting its declining health and mental state. The researcher makes a request to their superiors to suggest the dog be used for SAR work once again, this time for the Foundation. This portion of the article is told through an email.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ Show Hook/Attention-Grabber
- Hide Hook/Attention-Grabber

I want the reader to feel bad for this SCP. It’s just an animal born with powers it can’t quite control. The dog only wants to help people and be with its handler, but that can’t be because of the dangers present with its abilities.

Additional Notes:

+ Show Additional Notes
- Hide Additional Notes

My plan is to make this article fairly straightforward and short given that this is my first. I’m not expecting it to be greenlit quite yet, but I would appreciate any continued criticism or suggestion. In particular, whether the concept seems viable or whether I should rewrite the concept entirely.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlights) scpwiki.com
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

Elevator Pitch: scpwiki.com is a website created by The Foundation where creative writers post articles and tales detailing a fictional universe populated by anomalous items, entities and groups of interest, with the SCP Foundation at the heart.

Central Narrative: The Foundation created the website after online discussions of the SCP Foundation emerged, with the aim of protecting the masquerade by decieving people into believing it was fictional. However, a shift from SCP-507 reveals it to be anomalous, and responsible for creating events and anomalies in an alternate universe and its own SCP Foundation, leaving The Foundation to ponder if they are any different.

Hook/ Attention-Grabber: I want to ask a question that (please correct me if I'm wrong!) I haven't yet seen on the site; what if the Foundation exists in our world, and the site is merely for readers to be decieved into believing it does not exist? It fundamentally links our world and the fictional world in a very literal way.

Additional Notes: Again, I cannot say I am hugely well-read on the site, and so it is possible an article similar to this exists, for which I apologise- it is a coincidence. But I do believe that it has potential (and even considered storing it for when I had more experience writing and proposing it for 001, but I don't think it would stand its ground, and I'm impatient!).
